title: Budget Path in a Spending Category Tree
statement: A company's spending categories form a binary tree given in level-order array form: `tree` is a list where tree[0] is the root and the tree is reconstructed by scanning the array left to right, assigning each successive value as the left then right child of the next node still waiting for children (missing children are the value null). Each node's value is the dollar amount budgeted at that category. Given an integer `target`, determine whether there exists a root-to-leaf path (a path from the root down to a node with no children) whose node values sum exactly to `target`. An empty tree has no paths and should return false.
hints: This is a DFS-over-trees problem: explore each root-to-leaf path while tracking the remaining budget needed.
A node is a leaf when it has no left and no right child; only leaves can complete a valid path, so check the running sum exactly at leaves.

Recurse with a `remaining` amount: at a leaf, succeed if remaining equals the leaf's value; otherwise recurse into any existing children with remaining minus the current node's value, and return true if either branch succeeds.
